title: Compact-prefetch queue coordinator to reduce tail latency for console metrics streams
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Our console metrics pipeline has stable average latency, but a small fraction of requests (hotkeys and bursty tenants) experience large tail latency due to large queue growth and full-batch fetches. This results in delayed dashboards and missed alert windows for some customers.

Goal: Implement a compact-prefetch queue coordinator for the real-time ingest path that maintains small in-memory read-ahead buffers for hot keys, issues prioritized prefetches based on tenant/route activity, and enforces an occupancy-aware admission policy to keep tail latency within SLOs without sacrificing throughput. The coordinator should be pluggable into the existing ingest gateway and compatible with prefix/KV caching and our downstream partitioned stream processors.
acceptance_criteria: Tail p99 latency for console metrics ingest reduced by >= 40% for top 5% busiest tenants under burst load in the staging replay test
No more than 5% increase in overall CPU usage across ingest gateway under normal load
Coordinator exposes per-tenant queue depth, prefetch hit/miss, and backpressure signals to Console SLO dashboard
Can be toggled with runtime flags and rolled back with <5s failover time
Automated integration test that replays recorded burst waveform completes without dropped events and validates ordering guarantees
tasks: Design coordinator state machine and prefetch heuristics (draft design doc)
Implement in ingest gateway: compact ring buffer per-hotkey + occupancy estimator
Add admission controller enforcing occupancy thresholds and tenant-weighted fairness
Integrate metrics telemetry for queue_depth, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success, backpressure_count
End-to-end test harness: replay recorded production bursts and measure SLOs
Create migration/rollout plan with canary and gradual ramping by tenant
Code review and performance tuning (kernel selection and memory footprint)
